plan: [Third-price, 5 bidders: winner pays the 3rd-highest bid. With no past rounds and independent uniform values, I avoid risky overbidding that can cause negative payoff. Bidding my true value ($31) keeps me from ever paying more than my value while giving positive expected profit when the third-highest bid (determined by others) is below 31. This is a simple, robust best response under uncertainty for a one-shot game. ]

[I have value $31. With 4 opponents and no history, assume they bid their values. If I bid x I win with prob (x/49)^4 and, conditional on winning, the expected third-highest opponent value is 0.6x. Expected profit = (x/49)^4*(31−0.6x). Maximizing yields x=124/3≈41.33. Given 0.1 increments, bid $41.3 to maximize my expected payoff under this reasonable model.]

[Third-price auction: winner pays the 3rd-highest bid. With 5 bidders and values uniform 0–49, the expected 3rd-highest is about 24.5, well below my value 46, so winning yields positive expected surplus. To maximize long-run profit in this one-round game, I should aggressively secure the win by bidding above the maximum possible draw (49) to almost surely be highest, while accepting small chance others irrationally overbid. Bid slightly above 49 to capture the positive surplus.]

[This is a 5-bidder, third-price auction (winner pays the 3rd-highest bid). No prior history to learn from and values redraw each round. There is no dominant strategy; overbidding risks paying more than my value while underbidding loses profitable wins. To maximize long-run payoff given uncertainty, I will bid my true value ($20) to avoid negative surplus while keeping reasonable chance to win when opponents' bids are lower.]

[Third-price with 5 bidders: if I win I pay the second-highest of the other four. Conditional on being highest, other four are i.i.d. Uniform(0,v) so expected payment ≈ 0.6·v and expected surplus ≈ 0.4·v. With no history and symmetric opponents, truthful bidding (bid = value) is a natural safe equilibrium-like choice: it wins exactly when my value is highest and yields positive conditional surplus. I therefore bid my private value to maximize long-run profit under symmetry. ]
